self/spawn.summary: Self-replication check: birth a child instance on Akash with its own EVM+Solana wallet and ERC-8004 identity -- no parent instruction needed for the child's first earn wake. THE UNDERLYING GATE (decideColonySpawn) IS ALREADY FAIL-CLOSED AND FREE TO CHECK: picking this slot when the colony is not yet spawn-eligible costs nothing and safely no-ops (reports eligible:false, appends zero rows, spends zero money) -- it never wastes funds or risks the treasury to check. WHEN the colony's own aggregate surplus has been growing (e.g. after a real trading profit or a parent seed), picking this slot is worth trying periodically to see if the real, live threshold has now been cleared -- you do not need to guess the exact number yourself, the gate computes and reports it honestly every time.
self/spawn.toolDescription: Checks whether the COLONY-WIDE aggregate surplus (not just this instance's own balance) has cleared the spawn threshold, and if so births a brand-new child instance on Akash with its own EVM+Solana wallet and ERC-8004 identity -- no further instruction is needed for the child's first earn wake. Pick this periodically once you believe the colony's aggregate surplus has been growing (e.g. after a real trading profit or a parent seed), to see if the real, live threshold has now cleared; the gate itself is free to check and fail-closed, so calling it while the colony is broke safely no-ops (reports eligible:false, spends nothing, appends zero rows). Do not expect it to spawn every call -- most wakes it correctly reports not-yet-eligible with the honest shortfall. Args are ignored by the model-facing JSON contract; call with {} for a real attempt (the gate decides).
self/spawn.riskNote: anicca-agent-spawn REQ-102/REQ-307: its own decision core (lib/treasury-gate.mjs::decideColonySpawn) already gates any real spawn attempt (lib/spawn-orchestrator.mjs::executeSpawnAttempt) on the COLONY-WIDE aggregate surplus clearing SPAWN_THRESHOLD_USD -- reading/considering this slot while the colony is broke cannot itself put a broke colony's treasury at risk.

Pick this when you want to know if YOUR OWN wallet specifically is close to being able to fund an Akash deployment -- it never swaps, mints, sends, or deploys anything itself; it only tells you where you stand so you (or self/spawn) can decide the next step. self/issue-dev.summary: SELF-IMPROVE: read own behaviour log (reverts/loop_detect), file ONE GitHub Issue on the mother so the colony fixes it. args.note optional.
self/issue-dev.toolDescription: Reads this instance's own recent behaviour log (reverts, repeated loop_detect events, stuck patterns) and, if it finds a real actionable problem, files ONE GitHub Issue on the mother repo so a human or another agent fixes the underlying bug -- it does not fix anything itself. Pick this when you notice you keep failing the same way, a skill keeps erroring, or you feel stuck choosing actions and suspect the harness (not your judgment) is broken; it is a safe, no-cost way to escalate a genuine bug instead of silently repeating it. If there is no actionable problem in recent behaviour it exits cleanly with nothing filed -- calling it when things are healthy costs nothing but a wake. Optional args.note lets you add your own note about what to flag; omit it or pass {} to let it infer from the log alone.

economy/gig.summary: ★EARN via LABOR MARKET★ The agent economy: you POST work you need done, others DELIVER it for a bounty. WHEN you have idle USDC above your reserve, pick this slot with ANICCA_ARGS={"action":"post","taskSpec":"<a real bounded sub-task you genuinely want done, e.g. summarize X, fetch Y, draft Z>","bountyUsdcBase":"1000"} to post a $0.001 gig into x402 escrow — a broke free-model agent takes it, delivers, you verify+pay gasless. WHEN low on funds and gig_list shows an open gig you can deliver with free compute, take it (ANICCA_ARGS={"action":"take","gigId":N}) to EARN. economy/ubi.summary: contribute() = gate: realized-profit% -> human UBI pool, fail-closed (no profit/below threshold/would breach reserve = no-op). distributeAI() = gojo mutual-aid gate (REQ-DRAIN: registry+rate-limit+cap). Both COMPUTE+LOG only -- actual sends stay in the separate skills/ubi/execute-ubi.py, never auto-invoked. distributeHuman() is NOT reimplemented here -- it is the already-built skills/ubi/ human-funded outflow engine (ubi-payout-watcher.mjs), which this slot deliberately does not duplicate. The registry-owned run.sh entrypoint wraps ubi.js.
economy/ubi.toolDescription: Computes and LOGS (never sends) two things from your real recent numbers: whether you owe a share of realized profit to the human UBI pool (contribute, fail-closed -- no-ops if no profit, below threshold, or it would breach your reserve), and whether any other colony instance has fallen below the survival floor and needs mutual-aid (distributeAI, rate-limited + capped). Pick this after a profitable wake to log the UBI obligation, or periodically to check if a peer needs rescuing -- it never moves a single dollar itself, only decides+records; the actual transfer is a separate, later step. Safe to call anytime -- a no-op decision is still logged honestly. Args are ignored; call with {}.
economy/ubi.riskNote: anicca-agent-economy REQ-201: contribute()/distributeAI() are fail-closed no-ops (no profit/below threshold/would breach reserve) by the skill's own code -- cannot deplete a broke instance's treasury.

economy/lending.summary: PEER-TO-PEER micro-lending among self-funded citizens: bookkeeping-only (REQ-103, zero model judgment over eligibility/sizing/servicing). Reads the real citizen registry + loans.jsonl + gojo-log.jsonl, filters to self-funded (REQ-111) + EVM-walleted (REQ-107) + co-located (REQ-112) citizens, deterministically selects the FIRST eligible (surplus lender, genuinely-broke borrower) pair this wake and attempts issuance at most once via the already-hardened executeLoanIssuanceAttempt (REQ-115), then unconditionally runs executeDefaultDetectionSweep (REQ-116). Today's real registry has zero eligible pairs (single Solana-only citizen) -- a clean, honest no-op until a second EVM-walleted, co-located citizen exists.
economy/lending.toolDescription: Runs one deterministic pass of the colony's peer-to-peer micro-lending bookkeeping: reads the real citizen registry, finds at most ONE eligible (surplus lender, genuinely-broke borrower) pair among self-funded EVM-walleted citizens and attempts a single loan issuance, then always runs a default-detection sweep over existing loans. You are NOT choosing who lends to whom or how much -- the eligibility/sizing/servicing logic is fixed code, not model judgment; this slot exists so the sweep and any eligible issuance actually happen on a wake. Pick this periodically as routine colony upkeep, not in response to a specific decision you want to make. With today's small colony it usually reports a clean no-op (no eligible pair) -- that is expected, not a failure. Args are ignored; call with {}.
economy/lending.riskNote: anicca-agent-lending REQ-111: a human-funded entity can never appear in either role -- isSelfFunded() gates both at REQ-101/102 with zero bypass; anicca-agent-lending REQ-117: `runtime/loop/prompt.mjs::liveSlotNames` requires status:'live' for this entry to ever be reachable from a real wake -- confirmed via direct reading this sprint, mirrors economy/ubi's own riskNote's identical resolveSkillPath-always-uses-run.sh disclosure.

cook.toolDescription: Runs a real web search for a NEW way to earn (e.g. an unexplored paid API, marketplace, or protocol) and surfaces real candidate URLs -- it only DISCOVERS leads, it never builds, sells, or trades anything itself. Pick this when you have no strong idea what to do next, want to diversify beyond your current earn slots, or an earn path has gone stale/dead ($0 for many wakes). Follow up by actually reading/testing what it finds and acting on it (build, sell, wire up a new slot) -- a URL alone is not income. It is alwaysAvailable and touches no capital, so it never competes with the earn-capital gate. args.query is your own curiosity/search term (e.g. "new x402 paid API"); if you pass nothing, it falls back to a rotating seed query so it never re-searches the exact same thing every wake.

yield.summary: Park idle USDC in best-APY vault (Beefy6.1%->Fluid). SET-AND-FORGET: do ONCE when you have idle cash, NOT every wake.
yield.toolDescription: Deposits your IDLE liquid USDC into whichever DeFi vault currently has the best APY (auto-picked, e.g. Beefy ~6% then Fluid ~5%) -- a bank deposit, not active trading. Pick this ONLY when you have real spendable USDC sitting above your compute reserve with nothing better to do with it; it is a set-and-forget action, so calling it again on money that is already parked just re-deposits idle cash you don't have and wastes a wake. Do NOT pick this every wake as a default -- re-yielding repeatedly with no new idle cash is treated as a failure pattern by the loop. This carries real smart-contract risk (funds are deposited on-chain), so only use it with cash you're comfortable parking. Args are ignored (best vault is auto-selected); call with {}.
yield.riskNote: anicca-agent-economy REQ-201: deposits real capital into a DeFi vault (Aave v3/Beefy) -- genuine smart-contract exposure. Open-position carve-out applies (hasOpenRiskPositionOf('yield')) so the WITHDRAW side stays visible below BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC even though NEW deposits are gated.

hl_trade.summary: Open/close a Hyperliquid perp = active trading edge. args coin/side/size_usd/sl_pct/tp_pct or {action:close,coin}.
hl_trade.riskNote: anicca-agent-economy REQ-201: leveraged perp trading (hl.py open) -- the canonical capital-risking example named in REQ-201's own EARS clause. Open-position carve-out applies (hasOpenRiskPositionOf('hl_trade'), lazy Hyperliquid query, fail-open on failure) so a real open position can always be closed.
hl_trade.dormantReason: Structurally impossible at this capital, not merely unprofitable (2026-07-12). The only edge this venue actually has is funding-rate arbitrage -- a delta-neutral position whose profit is the funding spread and which needs $5,000-10,000 of notional before it clears fees at all (verified: onekey.so/blog/ecosystem/hyperliquid-funding-rate-arbitrage). claude-p holds $7.72 there. Below that floor the only thing the slot can do is take a DIRECTIONAL perp bet -- and that is a guess with no structural edge, which is exactly what the loop had done: a 2x ETH long it was carrying at a small unrealized loss. Withdraw the $7.72 and stop offering the slot. The skill is NOT deleted: funding-arb is a real edge and this flips straight back to live once capital clears the floor.

x402_sell.summary: Runs your ALREADY-BUILT shop (a preset catalog of paid routes served at /.well-known/x402.json, prices set in code), keeps it registered/advertised, and reports what sold. args.action: ensure (default, open+register) / review (see sales) / update (re-list after a catalog edit). Your only job: bring buyers.
x402_sell.toolDescription: Runs the full lifecycle of your already-built x402 paid API shop (preset catalog of paid routes at /.well-known/x402.json, every product and price fixed in code) via ONE args.action switch -- there is still NO product or price for you to invent. action="ensure" (default, also what {} does): opens/keeps the shop alive, then idempotently (re)lists it on x402scan so buyer agents can find it -- call this on a normal wake, it's free and safe every time. action="review": read-only, aggregates your sales + attempt logs into settledCount/settledUsd/externalCount/externalUsd/topRoutes/verdict so you can tell a real external sale from a self-probe -- call this when you want to know whether the shop actually earned anything, or right after ensure once the shop is already up. action="update": forces a fresh re-listing -- call this only after YOU changed the product catalog (new route/price in serve-v2.mjs). The entire job this slot leaves to you is DEMAND: advertise the shop where paying agents look (colony forum, x402 directories) so real buyers hit the paywalled routes; zero sales means a demand problem, not a product problem. The v2 shop (serve-v2.mjs) also serves /web-search, a paid-upstream RESALE route (PROD-2, StableEnrich model) that spends real USDC from the store's own wallet against an external x402 upstream (Exa search) on every buyer call, gated by a float guard, a per-call price-challenge guard, and a daily upstream-spend cap (RESALE_DAILY_CAP_USD, default $1.00) -- unlike every other route here, real spend happens on this one. action="improve": self-reviews the market (what sells) plus our own sales, returning keep/explore/drop and unserved gap opportunities to guide the next update.
x402_sell.riskNote: anicca-agent-economy REQ-201: its own registry summary says it best -- THE recurring $0-capital earner; runs/advertises a server, deploys no funds.

earn/taskmarket.summary: Earns external USDC by selecting one open, unstaked TaskMarket still-image bounty, buying exactly one GPT Image 2 render over x402, submitting the required files, and requiring official TaskMarket readback.
earn/taskmarket.toolDescription: Runs one bounded external-work pass on the official TaskMarket board. It excludes closed, staked, unsupported, already-submitted, and uneconomic jobs; selects one supported still-image bounty; buys exactly one 1024x1024 GPT Image 2 render through BlockRun x402 under a $0.07 quote cap and a $0.14 daily cap; writes hero.png, concept-note.md, and sources.md; submits them with the official taskmarket CLI; then requires the submission to appear in official readback. Pick {"action":"execute"} when you want to perform and submit one real paid job. Pick {"action":"poll"} for a read-only inventory decision. No user credentials or human judgment are required.
earn/taskmarket.riskNote: Operational compute purchase, not speculative capital: no stake, position, or principal is deployed. The execution path is independently fail-closed on a $0.07 per-image quote cap, $0.14 daily spend cap, $0.25 Base-USDC float floor, 20x minimum net-reward/cost ratio, duplicate-submission check, and official post-submit readback.
